about.title: About ETF Calculator - Exchange-Traded Fund Investment Analysis Tool
about.description: The ETF Calculator is a comprehensive investment analysis tool designed to help investors evaluate Exchange-Traded Fund investments, calculate returns, and compare ETF performance. Whether you're analyzing index ETFs, sector ETFs, or international funds, this calculator provides accurate projections for investment growth, expense ratios impact, and portfolio allocation strategies. Understanding ETF calculations is essential for building diversified investment portfolios and optimizing long-term returns.

faq.q: What's the difference between ETFs and mutual funds?
faq.a: ETFs trade like stocks throughout the day, typically have lower expense ratios, and are more tax-efficient due to in-kind redemptions. Mutual funds trade once daily at NAV and may have higher fees but offer automatic investing features.

faq.q: How do ETF expense ratios affect my returns?
faq.a: Expense ratios are annual fees that reduce your returns. A 0.1% difference in expense ratios can cost thousands over decades. For example, 0.05% vs 0.75% expense ratios on $100,000 over 30 years could differ by over $50,000 in total returns.

faq.q: Should I invest in broad market or sector-specific ETFs?
faq.a: Broad market ETFs (like total stock market or S&P 500) provide instant diversification and lower risk. Sector ETFs can enhance returns but add concentration risk. Most investors should use broad market ETFs as core holdings with sector ETFs as smaller allocations.

ETF dividends are typically paid in cash unless you enroll in a dividend reinvestment plan (DRIP) through your broker. Many brokers offer automatic dividend reinvestment for ETFs, which helps compound your returns over time.
